PullRequest.Title: chat: Refine customization discovery item targets
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- make the full Discover card and search result row the primary click and focus target
- keep Install and Installed actions layered above the item with independent behavior
- reduce marketplace icons from 48px to 40px
- preserve rounded corners for pointer and keyboard focus outlines

Fixes #338770

## After

![Discover customizations with compact icons and a rounded full-item focus outline](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7d37b8e9-487b-40e3-b387-2d9b9c48f126)

## Testing

- `npm run compile-client` — passed
- ESLint and Stylelint checks for the changed files — passed
- `git diff --check` — passed
- manually verified in a full authenticated Code OSS build with live marketplace icons

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Discover customizations browse view and render/click featured and grouped cards
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On a cold view, the existing marketplace query must complete before catalog cards render; the changed absolute primary-action overlay and sibling DOM placement add no asynchronous work. Marketplace icon images are lazy and are not required for card interaction. On a warm browse cache, cards render without a marketplace query.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query the customization marketplace for the browse catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request for an empty browse query with pageSize 100; subsequent empty-query renders use the per-source browseCatalogCache until invalidated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same marketplace query and cache path existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold catalog rendering waits for this request; warm cached rendering does not.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Assign lazy image URLs for marketplace icons, allowing the browser to fetch uncached icons.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one lazy image assignment per rendered card with a custom icon; browse presentation is bounded to up to 4 leading cards plus up to 4 cards for each of 3 type groups (16 total), with browser URL caching applying across duplicates/rerenders.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cards, icon URLs, lazy loading, and image count existed before the diff; only icon dimensions and DOM parent changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Icon fetches are lazy and do not block card construction or primary-action clicks.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Catalog size is fetched in a page of up to 100, while browse card rendering is bounded to 16 cards after grouping and leading-item selection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The marketplace query is a single request in this scenario. Lazy icon requests are browser-scheduled; the diff does not increase their count or concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Empty-query catalog pages are cached by selected source; browser image caching remains unchanged. The diff neither changes cache keys nor invalidation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that network, image, render cardinality, and cache behavior are unchanged; low confidence in any measurable regression from the CSS-only stacking change.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser paint cost from additional positioned stacking contexts is engine-dependent, but there is no evidence they create compositor layers or meaningful user-visible overhead at the bounded card count.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff changes hit targeting and icon size without adding boundary calls, item count, repeated layout reads, or retained resources.

Scenarios.Scenario: Search customizations, scroll virtualized results, and activate a result or its independent install action
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A debounced marketplace query supplies search results; WorkbenchList virtualizes row templates, and visible rows render their existing lazy icons. The changed full-row primary button is created once per virtualized template and removes the prior root click listener and focus/blur tracking listeners.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one request of 24 items per load; mixed-type filtered backfill can issue up to 8 sequential pages, and near-end scrolling schedules one continuation load at a time.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical query, pagination, cancellation, and continuation behavior existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initial result set waits for the query; continuation requests occur near the scroll boundary. Requests are cancelled/coalesced by the request token and schedulers.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Assign a lazy marketplace icon image for each rendered virtual row that has an icon URL.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One assignment per currently rendered/recycled row; browser caching applies by URL, and list virtualization limits live row templates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same icon helper was invoked per rendered row before the diff; moving the icon from inside the button to its sibling does not alter the URL, lazy flag, or render frequency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Lazy icons do not block list data rendering or row activation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Search result pages contain 24 resources and grow by pagination, but live DOM/template count remains viewport-bounded by WorkbenchList; effective network page concurrency is one.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Catalog loads are sequential and prior requests are cancelled on query changes; continuation uses a RunOnceScheduler. Icon loading is browser-managed and unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Search pages are not stored in the empty-query browse cache, while browser image caching remains available. The diff does not change cache behavior or negative-cache handling.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the renderer, WorkbenchList setup, scheduler, and icon helper that no hot/scaling work was introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The precise number of virtual rows depends on viewport overscan, but the diff removes three per-template listeners and does not increase row creation, network calls, or per-scroll work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: production changes reduce listeners and preserve virtualized rendering and boundary cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run the AI customization management component fixture assertions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The added assertions synchronously read card/result geometry and computed styles after the fixture has rendered. This is test-only execution and does not affect the product UI critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A constant number of geometry/style reads for the first featured card and first available result row per fixture invocation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous single fixture execution; no parallel boundary work is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the added getBoundingClientRect/getComputedStyle calls can force style/layout only in the component test harness.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Layout flush cost depends on the test browser state, but cardinality is constant and confined to tests.
Scenarios.Verdict: No user-visible performance regression: constant test-only synchronous layout reads do not affect shipped runtime behavior.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and all diff pages. Traced browse and search rendering, list virtualization, marketplace query pagination/caching, lazy icon loading, listener lifecycle, CSS layout changes, and fixture-only geometry reads. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced.
